summary: Spurs lined up in a 4-2-3-1 against Brentford's 4-2-3-1.
The result matched the chances: 0.57 xG to 3.87.

Compared with their other league games, Spurs conceded more (3.87 xG vs 0.85 xG), got into the box less (17 vs 31), settled for lower-quality chances (0.06 vs 0.08), went long less often (2.9% vs 3.7%).
Moore was the biggest attacking threat (0.40 xG + xA); Senesi won the ball back most often (6 tackles won + interceptions).

rows.label: Long balls, share of accurate passes

read: Spurs had 60% of the ball (season average 61%), completing 482 of 549 passes (88%).
68% of all passing in the opposition half was by Spurs (field tilt), in line with their usual 68%. They spent long spells camped in Brentford's half.
43% of Spurs' accurate passes were in their own half (208 own half, 274 opposition half): most of the passing happened high up the pitch.
Long balls made up 2.9% of accurate passes (in line with the season's 3.7%), with 42% of long balls finding a teammate. Spurs built short and rarely went direct.

phases.title: Chance creation
read: 9 shots (4 on target) worth 0.57 xG, 0.06 per shot; the season average is 0.08 per shot, so the chances were lower quality than usual.
4 shots came from inside the box and 5 from outside (56% from distance).
Spurs created 2 big chances and missed 2 (season average 2.0).
17 touches in Brentford's box, well below the season average of 31; Brentford had 39 in Spurs' box.
Where the xG came from: open play 0.44 (94%), fast breaks 0.00, set pieces 0.03. 7 of the shots came straight from a teammate's pass (assisted).

read: Spurs scored 0 from 0.57 xG: 0.6 fewer than the chances were worth.
Shots on target were worth 0.61 xGOT against 0.57 xG before the shot: placement was roughly average.

read: PPDA (estimated): 4.7 Brentford passes in their own half per Spurs defensive action; season average 4.2. Lower means a more aggressive press, so this was Spurs' usual pressing level.

Brentford managed 26 shots worth 3.87 xG (Spurs usually concede 0.85 xG) and 6 big chances.
